newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Electrabel volumes up 0.3 pct in Q1.
newsitem.headline: Electrabel volumes up 0.3 pct in Q1.

text.p: Belgian power utility Electrabel said on Monday its sales volumes rose 0.3 percent in the first quarter of this year against the first three months of 1996.

But the small overall rise hid a wide divergence between sales to industrial clients and those to domestic users, Finance and Marketing Director Willy Bosmans told a news conference after the company's annual general meeting.
He said sales volumes to industrial clients rose 5.1 percent against the first quarter of last year, while those to domestic users fell 2.4 percent.
The firm refused to give financial figures.
Chief Executive Jean-Pierre Hansen said that although 1997 had begun with the big freeze of January, it had become much milder much sooner than had been the case in 1996.

As an example he said that sales volumes had been 0.7 percent higher overall in January this year compared with January 1996, but that volumes in February had been 0.5 percent down from the same month the previous year.
He said it was impossible to extrapolate for the full year from the widely divergent volumes seen in the first quarter. It was also impossible to tell what might happen on tariffs and taxes.
